UnitStatement: DEL-11-05 (Contributor tutorial and onboarding) is a DOC_UPDATE deliverable under Package PKG-11 (Documentation, Examples, and Education).
DEL-11-05 covers scope item SOW-033 and supports objectives OBJ-001 and OBJ-002, with context envelope S.
DEL-11-05's lifecycle target for setup is SEMANTIC_READY after setup gates pass.
The primary purpose of DEL-11-05 is to create an onboarding path for new contributors using package/deliverable decomposition and governance docs.

DEL-11-05's production surface is deliverable-local setup/document production only; repo-level CONTRIBUTING, docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, documentation outside this deliverable, source code, and repo-level artifacts are excluded.
The intended audience is new contributors and Type 2 TASK workers needing a safe first path through OpenPipeStress governance, decomposition, and bounded execution.
Documentation targets are future CONTRIBUTING tutorial material and future AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW onboarding material, staged here only.
Public onboarding must not introduce protected standards text, copied tables, protected examples, proprietary vendor data, private rule packs, owner standards, or company design bases.
Onboarding must not state or imply that software, agents, maintainers, or contributors certify, approve, seal, authenticate, or declare engineering code compliance for reliance.
Type 2 work uses one sealed deliverable, explicit write scope, applicable invariants, acceptance criteria, and evidence.
Applicable architecture basis IDs are AB-00-01, AB-00-02, AB-00-06, AB-00-07, and AB-00-08; they inform contributor routing but do not mark PKG-00 as ISSUED.
Condition: use invented, public-domain, or permissively licensed examples only; otherwise record TBD or quarantine per policy (no protected examples).
Condition: contributor material must preserve user-supplied/private rule-pack and project-data boundaries (no public defaults for code data).
Condition: use "human review", "maintainer review", "acceptance gate", or "draft/proposal" language; avoid code-compliance certification claims.
Condition: this setup deliverable does not edit repo-level onboarding files; future integration must be a separate approved task or human action.
Condition: record TBD for unknowns; do not invent policy, legal conclusions, engineering values, or source citations.
The onboarding path should be constructed as a contributor journey with local drafting components.
Orientation component explains OpenPipeStress intent, agent roles, decomposition hierarchy, and sealed-deliverable execution; must remain descriptive and source-grounded.
Safe contribution checklist component lists protected-data, provenance, privacy, and professional-responsibility checks before public contribution; does not replace legal or professional review.

Type 2 task walkthrough component shows how a contributor reads _CONTEXT.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _STATUS.md, and register rows before working; does not authorize cross-deliverable edits.
Evidence and review handoff component describes expected outputs, validation evidence, warnings, and review readiness; does not mark any artifact accepted or ISSUED.
INIT.md provides bootstrap and stop-rule context (required reading order; agent rule).
AGENTS.md defines role and dispatch boundaries (agent posture; primary agents; dispatch rule).
docs/DIRECTIVE.md sections 1-6 provide project intent, boundaries, and stop rules.
docs/CONTRACT.md invariant index provides binding invariants.
docs/TYPES.md sections 1-9 provide IDs, statuses, epistemic labels, and authority vocabulary.
docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md sections 2-7 define public/private data and quarantine policy.

The contributor tutorial should make the first hour of contribution work predictable: read governing documents, locate the active deliverable, understand data and authority boundaries, work inside assigned scope, produce evidence, and hand off for review.
The tutorial is a path through the existing governance system, not a replacement for CONTRIBUTING, docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, or human review.
Principle: start with boundaries before mechanics; public code may implement open mechanics while protected standards and proprietary engineering data remain outside public defaults.
Principle: treat the decomposition as the work identity; a contributor works on one DEL-XX-YY inside one PKG-XX unless a human changes scope.
Principle: keep authority labels clear; Type 2 outputs are drafts/proposals until accepted, deterministic tools provide evidence not judgment, and humans resolve scope changes and acceptance gates.
Principle: prefer TBD over invention; missing policy choices, engineering values, source citations, or legal conclusions are surfaced rather than guessed.

Principle: keep examples clean; public examples are invented, original, public-domain, or permissively licensed with provenance and do not copy protected standards examples or commercial software cases.
Contributor path step: read INIT.md, AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/TYPES.md, docs/SPEC.md, and the active decomposition/register rows relevant to the assigned deliverable.
Contributor path step: confirm the sealed deliverable identity, package, scope items, objectives, invariants, acceptance criteria, and explicit write scope.
Contributor path step: inspect _CONTEXT.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, and _STATUS.md before changing production artifacts.
Contributor path step: make only scoped edits and record evidence through validation commands, warnings, and open issues.
Contributor path step: return a handoff with changed paths, validation results, data-boundary notes, and review readiness.

The public repository may contain schemas, mechanics, workflows, blank templates, and invented or permissively licensed examples, but not protected standards text/tables/examples, copied code formulas, proprietary vendor catalogs without rights, private owner standards, private rule packs, or company design bases.
If a source appears protected, the contributor should stop, mark the concern, and escalate through the project review path rather than paraphrase it.
A maintainer can accept a development artifact, but that is not a professional engineering approval of a piping calculation.
A user rule-check result is not a professional code-compliance declaration; software output remains decision support until a competent human accepts it for a particular project.
SCA-001 allows PKG-00 SEMANTIC_READY content to be used as an architecture-basis candidate for sealed brief injection.
Contributors should use applicable basis IDs as context constraints, especially the no-bypass API/adapter baseline, without treating PKG-00 as ISSUED or copying full PKG-00 prose into new artifacts.
Trade-off (helpful tutorial vs over-specific process): provide a concrete path through existing files, but keep repo-level publication and policy decisions separate from this deliverable.
Trade-off (contributor confidence vs certification language): explain what maintainers review and what tools check, but avoid any statement that software or agents approve engineering work.
Trade-off (rich examples vs IP risk): use invented examples and provenance notes rather than real protected code examples or commercial software files.

Trade-off (automation vs human authority): use scripts for evidence and repeatability while preserving human gates for scope, acceptance, legal/professional questions, and ambiguous protected content.
Safe onboarding example: confirm DeliverableID, PackageID, Scope Coverage, Objective Support, write scope, and applicable invariants from _CONTEXT.md before editing.
The safe onboarding step is a process example only and does not introduce engineering values or standards material.
Unsafe onboarding example: copying a code example from a standard or commercial report and adapting it into public docs.
Copying a standard/commercial code example into public docs violates the protected-content boundary unless documented redistribution rights and human/legal review explicitly allow it.
No source conflicts were detected during setup.

If future repo-level onboarding asks this deliverable to edit CONTRIBUTING or docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md directly, that is a scope change from this setup session and must be routed for human approval.
This procedure defines how to produce and verify the contributor onboarding tutorial draft for DEL-11-05 inside the deliverable working folder.
Prerequisite: the contributor has read the assigned brief and confirmed the write scope is only this deliverable folder.
Prerequisite: _CONTEXT.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _STATUS.md, and register rows for DEL-11-05 and SOW-033 are available.
Prerequisite: governing references listed in _REFERENCES.md are accessible for reading.
Prerequisite: no protected standards examples, proprietary vendor data, private rule packs, owner standards, or commercial software examples are imported.
Prerequisite: the current lifecycle state allows setup refresh.
Step 1: confirm deliverable identity by reading _CONTEXT.md and verifying Deliverable ID DEL-11-05, Package ID PKG-11, Type DOC_UPDATE, Scope Coverage SOW-033, and Objective Support OBJ-001; OBJ-002.

Step 2: confirm source authority by reading INIT.md, AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/TYPES.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, and the decomposition/register rows listed in _REFERENCES.md.

Step 3: draft the contributor tutorial concept across the four-document kit, placing identity/boundaries/references in Datasheet.md, normative requirements/invariants/acceptance in Specification.md, rationale/trade-offs/examples in Guidance.md, and execution/validation steps in Procedure.md.
Step 4: preserve hard boundaries by not editing repo-level CONTRIBUTING, docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, source code, examples, schemas, or documentation outside this deliverable.

Step 4: do not introduce protected standards text, copied standards tables, code-derived formulas, commercial software examples, proprietary vendor data, private rule packs, owner standards, or company design bases.
Step 4: do not claim software, agents, contributors, or maintainers certify, approve, seal, authenticate, or declare engineering code compliance.
Step 5: generate setup artifacts in sequence: four-documents RUN_PASSES=P1_P2, semantic-matrix-build, lens-register, four-documents RUN_PASSES=P3_ONLY, then dependency-extract.

Step 6: validate setup gates by running check_min_viable_fileset.sh, check_four_documents.sh, validate_dependencies_schema.py on Dependencies.csv, validate_enum.py LIFECYCLE_STATE SEMANTIC_READY, and scanning local artifacts for protected-data risk and certification/compliance-claim language.
Step 7: if all setup gates pass, update _STATUS.md to SEMANTIC_READY; if any gate fails, leave status below SEMANTIC_READY, record the failure in _run_records, and surface open issues.
Step 8: return the handoff reporting status, changed paths, validation commands/results, warnings, and open issues.

The setup is valid when all required files exist, dependency schema validation passes, the semantic lens and lensing register exist, run records are present, no out-of-scope file is modified, and _STATUS.md is set to SEMANTIC_READY only after those checks pass.

Required setup records include Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, _SEMANTIC.md, _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md, Dependencies.csv, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _STATUS.md, and _run_records/TASK_RUN_*.md.

DEL-11-05 defines a contributor onboarding tutorial draft inside the working folder covering orientation to OpenPipeStress governance, package/deliverable decomposition, sealed Type 2 execution, evidence production, review handoff, and protected-data boundaries.

This setup run does not edit repo-level CONTRIBUTING, docs/AGENTIC_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, documentation outside this deliverable, source code, examples, schemas, or release artifacts; future repo-level publication requires a separate approved task or human action.
REQ-11-05-01: the tutorial draft shall start contributors from root bootstrap and governance reading before any implementation or documentation work.
REQ-11-05-02: the tutorial draft shall explain the flat package/deliverable hierarchy and stable ID model used by OpenPipeStress.
REQ-11-05-03: the tutorial draft shall describe Type 1 and Type 2 agent responsibilities without expanding TASK authority beyond a sealed deliverable.
REQ-11-05-04: the tutorial draft shall require contributors to preserve protected standards, vendor IP, private data, and provenance controls.
REQ-11-05-05: the tutorial draft shall preserve the rule-pack boundary: public examples use invented non-code values and user/code data remains user supplied.
REQ-11-05-06: the tutorial draft shall preserve professional responsibility boundaries and avoid certification, code-compliance, approval, sealing, or reliance claims by agents/software.
REQ-11-05-07: the tutorial draft shall tell contributors to use architecture-basis constraints only as dispatch context and not as ISSUED product authority.
REQ-11-05-08: the tutorial draft shall include evidence expectations: changed paths, validation commands/results, warnings, open issues, and review handoff.
REQ-11-05-09: the setup artifacts shall include four documents, semantic matrix, lensing register, dependency register, run records, and final status only if setup gates pass.
No engineering design standard content is used as source material for this contributor tutorial; governing standards are the project governance and workflow documents listed in _REFERENCES.md.

If a future contributor wants to include any standard, vendor, owner, or commercial software material in onboarding examples, the correct action is to stop and route the material through protected-content/provenance review rather than copy or paraphrase it.
Verification: four-document presence check (check_four_documents.sh) must return PASS.
Verification: minimum metadata presence check (check_min_viable_fileset.sh) must return PASS.
Verification: dependency schema check (validate_dependencies_schema.py on Dependencies.csv) must return VALID.
Verification: lifecycle enum check (validate_enum.py LIFECYCLE_STATE SEMANTIC_READY) must return VALID.
Verification: protected-data boundary scan must find no protected standards tables, code examples, proprietary vendor data, private rule packs, or commercial software examples introduced.
Verification: professional-claims scan must find no automatic compliance, certification, approval, sealing, or professional reliance claim by software or agents.
Verification: semantic setup requires _SEMANTIC.md Audit Result PASS and _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md coverage rows for matrices A, B, C, F, D, X, and E.
Required setup outputs are Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, _SEMANTIC.md, _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md, Dependencies.csv, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _run_records/*, and _STATUS.md.
Repo-level publication targets remain references only in this setup session.
Invariant OPS-K-IP-1/2/3: public onboarding content must exclude protected standards/vendor/commercial/private material and must require provenance review for public data.
Invariant OPS-K-DATA-1/2/3: code-specific and proprietary engineering data are user supplied or private; missing values stay explicit.
Invariant OPS-K-RULE-1/3: public rule-pack examples are invented/non-code and rule packs carry version, checksum, source notes, and public/private markers where referenced.
Invariant OPS-K-AUTH-1: no software or agent certification, approval, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance reliance claim.
Invariant OPS-K-PRIV-1/2: private project/code/rule/component data and telemetry boundaries stay visible.
Invariant OPS-K-AGENT-1 through OPS-K-AGENT-4: contributors and agents do not invent facts, conflicts are surfaced, Type 2 work is sealed, and outputs are drafts until accepted.
Invariant no-bypass adapter/API baseline: contributors touching plugins/adapters/API topics must preserve units, provenance, diagnostics, rule sandboxing, report controls, and data-boundary checks.

DEL-11-05 setup is ready for review when the listed setup artifacts exist, validation commands pass, no protected-data or certification-claim warning is found in local artifacts, and _STATUS.md records Current State: SEMANTIC_READY.
